title: 1999 AMC 8 Problem 16
statement:
Tori’s mathematics test had \(75\) problems: \(10\) arithmetic, \(30\) algebra, and \(35\) geometry problems. Although she answered \(70\%\) of the arithmetic, \(40\%\) of the algebra, and \(60\%\) of the geometry problems correctly, she did not pass the test because she got less than \(60\%\) of the problems right.

How many more problems would she have needed to answer correctly to earn a \(60\%\) passing grade?

solutions.text:
She answered \( 10 \cdot 0.7 = 7 \) arithmetic questions correctly. She answered \( 30 \cdot 0.4 = 12 \) algebra ones correctly. She also got \(35 \cdot 0.6 = 21 \) geometry questions correctly.

This means she got a total of \( 7 + 12 + 21 = 40 \) questions correct.

As such, in order to get a \(60\%,\) Tori must have answered \[ 75 \cdot 0.6 = 45 \] questions correctly. This means that she would have needed to answer an additional \(45 - 40 = 5\) questions correctly.

Thus, B is the correct answer.
